assertions.observed: 0016_reservations_foundation.sql lines 802-829 define rsv_occupancy_no_overlap_insert and rsv_occupancy_no_overlap_update exactly as specified: BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE ON rsv_table_occupancies, WHEN NEW.active = 1 AND NEW.overbook = 0, SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'rsv_table_occupancies overlap') WHERE EXISTS (same o.table_id, o.active=1, o.overbook=0, o.start_at < NEW.end_at AND o.end_at > NEW.start_at); the update variant excludes the row itself (o.id <> NEW.id). The passing schema test 'enforces table occupancy overlap triggers and allows back-to-back, overbook = 1, and active = 0 (VAL-FND-011)' asserts: (1) overlapping INSERT [1500,2500) over base [1000,2000) rejects with the exact message 'rsv_table_occupancies overlap'; (2) adjacent inserts [2000,3000) and [500,1000) succeed (boundary-touching passes); (3) overlapping UPDATE into [1800,2500) rejects with the same message, while widening the row's own window succeeds; (4) overlapping INSERT with overbook=1 succeeds, and an overbook=0 row may even overlap an overbook=1 row on insert and update; (5) overlapping INSERT with active=0 succeeds, and reactivating that inactive row rejects. Cross-check: both real tenant DBs (acme, riyadh-grill) list rsv_occupancy_no_overlap_insert and rsv_occupancy_no_overlap_update in sqlite_master (9 rsv_* triggers total in each).
assertions.limitations: Real-DB trigger presence is an observation on the two seeded orgs, not the pass criterion; the criterion (migration SQL + schema test) is fully verified. Test evidence is the passing Vitest run, not a standalone sqlite3 replay outside the suite.

assertions.observed: Hold single-conversion: rsv_holds_single_conversion (0016 lines 831-835) is BEFORE UPDATE ON rsv_holds WHEN OLD.status = 'converted' -> RAISE(ABORT, 'hold_already_converted'); the passing test asserts the first conversion ('converted' + reservation_id) succeeds, a second/conflicting conversion aborts with 'hold_already_converted', and any other status change from 'converted' also aborts. rsv_reservations.hold_id is UNIQUE via CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uniq_rsv_reservations_hold_id ON rsv_reservations (hold_id) (0016 line 531); the test asserts a second reservation with the same hold_id rejects with UNIQUE, and the index exists in both real tenant DBs. Append-only: rsv_reservation_events_no_delete and rsv_audit_log_no_delete are unconditional BEFORE DELETE triggers (RAISE(ABORT,'append_only')); _no_update variants abort unless the update sets data/changes = '{"redacted":true}' with id (+reservation_id +type for events; +entity_id +action for audit) unchanged; rsv_guest_merges_no_delete/_no_update abort unconditionally. The passing test asserts: event DELETE rejects, arbitrary event UPDATE rejects, event redaction that also mutates type rejects, plain event redaction succeeds and reads back as {redacted:true}; audit DELETE rejects, audit mutation rejects, audit redaction succeeds and reads back as {redacted:true}; guest-merge DELETE and UPDATE both reject. Both real tenant DBs list all 9 rsv_* triggers including rsv_holds_single_conversion, the event/audit/merge append-only pairs.
assertions.limitations: hold_id UNIQUE is a named unique index rather than a column-level UNIQUE constraint; the guarantee is equivalent (NULL hold_id rows unaffected) and the test verifies the UNIQUE rejection on duplicate conversion. Real-DB trigger presence is an observation on the two seeded orgs; the criterion (migration SQL + schema test) is fully verified.
